sentences.en: In the morning it was overcast, and we planned to go watch a match in the afternoon.
My colleague said: "It's definitely going to rain this afternoon."
I said: "Not necessarily — the weather forecast is sometimes wrong too."
He said he'd watched the news, and the news said there would be heavy rain today.

t: when it got to; by the time it was
sentences.en: By the afternoon, the weather had gradually improved, and it hadn't rained after all.
My colleague glanced outside and said: "I didn't expect it really wouldn't rain today."
We arrived, and the match was just starting.

quiz.q: What does the colleague predict in the morning?
a: It will be sunny all day

quiz.q: How does the narrator respond to the prediction?
a: Says 不一定 because forecasts can be wrong
Says he already checked the news

quiz.q: What actually happens by the afternoon?
a: The weather clears up and the match starts on time

grammar.e: 不一定 says something isn't certain or doesn't always hold — a mild way to disagree with someone's absolute claim.
grammar.x: 不一定，天气预报有时候也会错。— Not necessarily, the weather forecast is sometimes wrong too.

grammar.p: 到了 + time word (by the time X came)
grammar.e: 到了 followed by a time word marks reaching that point in time, often to introduce a change that happened by then.
grammar.x: 到了下午，天气慢慢变好，也没有下雨。— By the afternoon, the weather had gradually improved, and it hadn't rained after all.

grammar.e: 没想到 introduces something that turned out differently from what was expected.
grammar.x: 没想到今天真的没下雨。— I didn't expect it really wouldn't rain today.
